section_summary.extract_value: This section, titled 'The Two Faces of Self-Esteem', discusses self-esteem as a widely studied psychological construct, primarily assessed using the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES). It explores the common belief that high self-esteem is beneficial, noting its association with positive affect, but also highlights emerging concerns about its problematic correlates, such as increased willingness to experiment with alcohol and drugs, bullying behavior, proneness to violence under ego-threat, and self-enhancement. The text refers to findings from numerous existing studies and reviews, but does not present any new, distinct, or numbered studies within this paper.
